title: Smooth exceptional Künneth transpose identity
statement:
Use the finite-field datum and $A=A_{E,n}$ with the actual operations of [sk-def-sf-operations]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $Z$ be separated of finite type over $k$. Put $F=f\times\mathrm{id}_Z$, $r:X\times Z\to X$, $s:Y\times Z\to Y$, and $\omega_f=Rf^!A_Y$. Write $\theta_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes^L\omega_f\to Rf^!K$ and $b:r^*\omega_f\to\omega_F$ for the specified counit-transpose maps of [def-pur-co-smoothness](2),(3), which are invertible by [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness]. For all $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ and $Q\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$, the composite
$$Rf^!K\boxtimes Q\xrightarrow{\theta_{f,K}^{-1}\boxtimes1}LF^*(K\boxtimes Q)\otimes^Lr^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{1\otimes b}LF^*(K\boxtimes Q)\otimes^L\omega_F\xrightarrow{\theta_{F,K\boxtimes Q}}RF^!(K\boxtimes Q)$$
(with the canonical monoidal pullback and symmetry identifications) equals the specified $\alpha_{f,\mathrm{id}_Z}(K,Q)$ of [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](ii). This is an equality of natural transformations.

source.place: alpha: smooth purity, smooth trace as exceptional counit, and its base-change square

proof.text: Abbreviate $P_h=Rh_!$, $U_h=Lh^*$, $\omega=\omega_f$, $H=U_fK\otimes^L\omega$, and $W=K\boxtimes Q$. Write $t:Y\times Z\to Z$. Use the canonical identity adjunction to identify $R\operatorname{id}_Z^!Q$ with $Q$. The finite-coefficient stability theorem, clauses (i),(ii),(iv),(v), puts all pullbacks, tensors, compact-support images and exceptional images below in $D^b_{ctf}$. The specified smooth tensor map $T=\theta_{f,K}\boxtimes1_Q:H\boxtimes Q\to Rf^!K\boxtimes Q$ is an isomorphism by cohomological smoothness. Set $\rho:H\boxtimes Q\xrightarrow{\sim}U_FW\otimes^LU_r\omega$ to be the signed reassociation. It suffices to compare the two proposed maps after precomposition by $T$.

source.place: Definition 5.1 (specified tensor and base-change transposes); Remark 3.13 (target-module coherence)

proof.text: For any $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ put $E_M:U_sP_fM\to P_FU_rM$ and $C_{M,Q}=(E_M^{-1}\otimes1)\operatorname{PF}_{F,U_rM,U_tQ}^{-1}$, as in the cited exterior module lemma. This is precisely $\mathrm{Ku}_{!,f,\operatorname{id}_Z}(M,Q)$. Indeed in the relative-product definition over $B=Y\times Z$, the two maps to $B$ are $F:X\times Z\to B$ and $\operatorname{id}_B:B\to B$, with inputs $U_rM,U_tQ$. Its first nonidentity arrow is $\operatorname{PF}_{F,U_rM,U_tQ}^{-1}$ and the product-square exchange contributes $E_M^{-1}$; the projection formula and composition maps for $\operatorname{id}_B$ are identities, and the final two symmetries cancel. Thus the transpose of the specified $\alpha_{f,\operatorname{id}_Z}$ is $(\varepsilon_{f,K}\boxtimes1_Q)C_{Rf^!K,Q}$. Naturality of $C$ makes its precomposition with $P_F(T)$ equal to $((\varepsilon_{f,K}P_f\theta_{f,K})\boxtimes1_Q)C_{H,Q}$.

source.place: Definition 5.1 (specified tensor and base-change transposes); Remark 3.13 (target-module coherence)

proof.text:
Put $e=\varepsilon_{f,A_Y}:P_f\omega\to A_Y$. The definition of $\theta_{f,K}$ gives the exact identity $\varepsilon_{f,K}P_f\theta_{f,K}=(e\otimes1_K)\operatorname{PF}_{f,\omega,K}^{-1}P_f(\sigma)$, where $\sigma:U_fK\otimes\omega\to\omega\otimes U_fK$. Substitute this in step 2. Apply the exterior module identity with $M=\omega$, keeping its signed reordering of $K$ and $Q$. Expanding $C_{\omega,Q}$ gives the resulting transpose
$$a=(U_se\otimes1_W)(E_\omega^{-1}\otimes1_W)\operatorname{PF}_{F,U_r\omega,W}^{-1}P_F(\sigma\rho).$$
Here $\sigma\rho:H\boxtimes Q\to U_r\omega\otimes U_FW$ first applies $\rho$ and then swaps its two factors. The cited module identity already includes extracting both target factors as the single object $W$. Applied after the displayed swap of $U_fK$ and $\omega$, its $\zeta$ is exactly $\sigma\rho$, so it gives the displayed formula directly.

source.place: Definition 5.1 (specified tensor and base-change transposes); Remark 3.13 (target-module coherence)

proof.text:
Let $v=\theta_{F,W}(1\otimes b)\rho:H\boxtimes Q\to RF^!W$, the proposed composite after precomposition by $T$. Its exceptional transpose is
$$\varepsilon_{F,W}P_F(v)=(\varepsilon_{F,A}P_Fb\otimes1_W)\operatorname{PF}_{F,U_r\omega,W}^{-1}P_F(\sigma\rho).$$
To see this, insert the counit-transpose defining formula for $\theta_{F,W}$ from condition (2) of cohomological smoothness. Move $P_F(b\otimes1)$ through the inverse projection formula by naturality in its first argument. This leaves the displayed composite, with exactly the same signed symmetry as in step 3; it does not choose an orientation or replace a specified map by an unspecified isomorphism.

source.place: Definition 5.1 (specified tensor and base-change transposes); Remark 3.13 (target-module coherence)

proof.text:
Condition (3) in the definition of cohomological smoothness defines $b$ by its transpose in the Cartesian square $(F,r,f,s)$. Consequently
$$\varepsilon_{F,A}P_Fb=U_se\circ E_\omega^{-1}.$$
Substitution in step 4 makes its transpose exactly $a$ from step 3. Thus $v$ and $\alpha_{f,\operatorname{id}_Z}T$ have the same transpose under the actual constructible exceptional adjunction $P_F\dashv RF^!$. Its Hom bijection is injective; hence they are equal. Cancel the isomorphism $T$ from step 1 to obtain the asserted equality, including the inverse $\theta_{f,K}^{-1}$ in its stated position.

source.place: Definition 5.1 (specified tensor and base-change transposes); Remark 3.13 (target-module coherence)

proof.text: The identities above hold for arbitrary $K,Q$ and are natural: $C$, the projection maps, the exchanges, $\theta$ and $b$ are natural in their inputs, and tensor reassociation and symmetry are natural. Inverting the natural isomorphism $\theta_{f,-}$ preserves naturality. The component equality therefore is the required equality of natural transformations.

I read the item, the new node, every cited statement, the parent sk-thm-sf-kunneth-verdier step 4 (the only node citing the item), the unit record, the main-20261015 alpha paragraph, and Scholze Six-Functor Formalisms Remark 3.13 (p. 24) and Definition 5.1 (p. 32). The item's statement is unchanged and is exactly what the parent's step 4 uses. theta and b are the counit transposes of def-pur-co-smoothness(2),(3), which match Scholze Def. 5.1; they are invertible by thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness, whose statement depends on def-pur-co-smoothness. The coefficient category is finite A_{E,n} with D^b_ctf throughout. No SGA source is cited, and the item is not a target node. Step 2 is right: Ku_{!,f,id_Z} reduces to PF_{F,U_rM,U_tQ}^{-1} (sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative clause (iv)) followed by E_M^{-1}, so the transpose of alpha is (eps⊠1)C. Step 3 combines the theta formula, naturality of C and the new lemma with M=omega. The two canonical isomorphisms zeta(sigma⊠1) and sigma∘rho have the same underlying permutation and are equal by symmetric-monoidal coherence. Step 4 follows from the theta formula for F and naturality of PF^{-1} in its first argument. Step 5 uses def-pur-co-smoothness(3) on the square (F,r,f,s), eps_F P_F b = U_s e∘E_omega^{-1}, and injectivity of the constructible Hom bijection of thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class(2). I tested the item with Z=pt, Q=A and with f=id; both sides agree. The new node lem-sf-exterior-shriek-projection-compatibility type-checks and is true: it is PF base-change compatibility plus the D(Y)-linear coherence of Remark 3.13. Tested with f=id, Z=pt, K=A and zero inputs, with no counterexample. It contains no f^!, theta or smoothness, so it does not restate the item.
